name: Carlo Ancelotti

spellsCounted.reason: Champions League 2002-03 and 2006-07, Serie A 2003-04; Christmas tree 4-3-2-1 with Pirlo as regista
Premier League and FA Cup 2009-10; 4-4-2 diamond / 4-3-2-1
Champions League 2013-14; 4-3-3 with Di Maria as left-sided 8, counter-attacking
La Liga and Champions League 2021-22, 2023-24; low block + counter, fluid 4-4-2 / 4-3-1-2

scopeNote: Ancelotti across six counted spells (Milan 2001-09, Chelsea 2009-11, PSG 2011-13, Real Madrid 2013-15, Bayern 2016-17, Real Madrid 2021-25). Exact days: only 2013-06-25 (Real Madrid appointment, Wikipedia) and 2021-06-01 (second Real Madrid start, LaLiga Expert) were read in a source; the other days (Milan 2001-11-06 start and 2009-06-30 end, Chelsea 2009-06-01 and sacking 2011-05-22, PSG 2011-12-30, Real Madrid exit 2015-05-25 and 2025-05-25, Bayern 2016-07-01 start and sacking 2017-09-28) are from general knowledge and not verified in a fetched page, so treat them as partial. The 'Christmas tree' (albero di Natale) is the 4-3-2-1 used at Milan 2006-07 and briefly Chelsea 2009-10; before that Milan used 4-3-1-2/4-4-2 diamond. At Real Madrid he is described as relational/fluid (4-3-3 shifting to 4-4-2 / 4-3-1-2), not as a positional-play coach. Coaches' Voice, TFA and Medium analyses cover mostly Real Madrid 2021-24; Milan, Chelsea, PSG and Bayern tactics rest mainly on Coaches' Voice overviews, Wikipedia and Bayern-fan press. Marking: open play is zonal-based with man-oriented pieces (two CBs tight on striker; man-to-man at goal kicks); corners are zonal line plus blockers (TFA). No Milan-era marking or set-piece source was found. Excluded-spell dates are year-only (user-decided, not researched). The UEFA mid-block entry has a placeholder articleDate (page unreadable, unverified).
openQuestions: Exact start and end days for Milan, Chelsea, PSG, Bayern and Real Madrid exit dates not confirmed in a fetched page.
Manhattan Institute article date is unknown; text (56 years old, 'new boss of Bayern') implies 2016, set to 2016-10-01 as placeholder.
Wikipedia says Ancelotti used 3-4-1-2 at Juventus; Coaches' Voice and The National say 4-3-2-1 / 4-1-3-2 (Juventus is excluded from counted spells).
Shape at the 2007 Athens final: 4-3-2-1 (Wikipedia, Coaches' Voice) vs 4-4-2 on one fan lineup site.
Ancelotti said 'we won't change the 4-3-3' (Oct 2021) but later said he does not know whether the 2022 final was 4-3-3 or 4-4-2: tension between stated rigidity and fluid practice.
Milan-era pressing, marking and set-piece behaviour lack a tier A-B source; UEFA and Sky Italia pages could not be read.
Quiet Leadership quotes come through a secondary review; check the book text for exact wording.

statedView.quote: In my fist couple of coaching jobs at Reggiana then Parma I played very rigid 4-4-2. I was of the mind the players had to fit into the system and the first priority was to set the team up defensively. But when I arrived at Juventus I changed my view and that was because of Zidane.
If you have a lot of quality in terms of attacking players then that is what you must devise your tactics around. [...] get the shape to suit the players.
With Gareth Bale and Cristiano Ronaldo, the best system is 4-3-3.
statedView.source: Gazzetta dello Sport, as reported by Football España (book 'Il mio albero di Natale', 2013)

statedView.quote: The counter-attack is the simplest way of creating a scoring opportunity. Clearly just using the counter means you don't have an identity, but when there's space for it with the strikers we've got, it becomes lethal.
statedView.source: Gazzetta dello Sport, as reported by Football España

statedView.quote: The main change is we press a bit more intermittently and we try to play more directly, more vertically.
statedView.source: Wikipedia citing Bayern-era interview (original not located)

statedView.quote: In football, as in anything, you must not stand still. Never believe that the tactics you deploy today and that have brought you great success will continue to be effective tomorrow.
statedView.source: Quiet Leadership (Penguin, 2016) as quoted by Manhattan Institute

statedView.quote: I treat them like people first, not just like players. I want to speak to them at the same level.
statedView.source: Interview with Alex Reid of Sport, quoted in Manhattan Institute review of Quiet Leadership

statedView.quote: Our pressing isn't too high up. We like it that way; with a lower block, you have the chance to use the forwards on the counter.
statedView.source: Coaches' Voice, after Real Madrid 2-0 Atletico
Press conference after Espanyol defeat, reported by LaLiga Expert 2022-03-29

statedView.quote: If you asked me how we played the final in Paris, 4-3-3 or 4-4-2, I will tell you I do not know.

If Vinicius or Rodrygo feel more comfortable opening up a little more on the wings when the team has the ball, I am not going to tell them to stay inside, because it is an individual interpretation of the game.
statedView.source: Sky Sports, 2024-05-29 (also Wikipedia: The Times interview before 2024 final)

statedView.quote: Mi idea era meter a los centrocampistas con energía para presionar arriba, mantener un ritmo alto y evitar contraataques.
statedView.source: Real Madrid official press conference after Leipzig

statedView.quote: I am not an obsessive person. I like football a lot, it's a passion of mine, but I try to keep things as simple as possible. Football for me isn't complicated.
